caption:
Both paths get people promoted. The cost is paid at different times.

Staying frontend compounds. Two more years of depth makes you the person people pull into the hardest UI problems, and that's hard to replace.

Switching costs you some speed and standing for a few months. But year 2 is the cheapest it will ever be: your salary and title haven't locked you in yet, and you bring a frontend view backend and AI teams often lack.

There's a middle road too: frontend for AI features, like streaming chat UIs.

What would you pick, and what would make you switch?
